Article Title: 'He can remove Pakistan from world picture': Shinde on PM Modi's cropped SCO photo
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde criticised Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s Office for cropping Prime Minister Narendra Modi out of a photograph from the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, saying Pakistan should not attempt to “play such games” with India.“What Pakistan has done is extremely unfortunate. Pakistan has always attempted such things. However, I would say that while they may have removed Modi Ji’s photograph, if Modi Ji wants, he can remove Pakistan from the world picture,” Shinde said on Tuesday.His remarks came after Sharif’s office shared an edited version of the SCO family photograph that placed the Pakistani prime minister at the centre while cropping out several leaders. The original photograph, taken before a session of the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, showed the heads of member states standing together.“During Operation Sindoor, terrorists in Pahalgam committed a grave crime against our people and our sisters by wiping away their sindoor. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, our armed forces completely destroyed terrorist bases in Pakistan. They also destroyed 11 airbase camps and brought Pakistan to its knees,” he said.“The entire country is proud of the Indian armed forces and Prime Minister Modi’s leadership. Therefore, Pakistan should never attempt to play such games with our country,” Shinde added.He also said that editing Modi out of the photograph would not affect his standing in India or internationally.“I would also say that such an act of removing a photograph cannot erase Prime Minister Modi from the hearts of 140 crore Indians. In fact, Prime Minister Modi remains one of the most popular leaders in the world...”The 26th SCO summit, which marked the organisation’s 25th anniversary, focused on regional cooperation as well as security, economic and geopolitical challenges. The summit was held in the expanded “SCO Plus” format, bringing together leaders from member, partner and observer countries.Addressing the summit, PM Modi called for a united fight against terrorism and said there could be no “double standards” on the issue. He called for the dismantling of the “entire ecosystem of terrorism”, including its financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.
Article Summary: Eknath Shinde criticised Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s Office for cropping Prime Minister Narendra Modi out of a photograph from the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. His remarks came after Sharif’s office shared an edited version of the SCO family photograph that placed the Pakistani prime minister at the centre while cropping out several leaders.

Article Title: Ram temple cash theft: Journalist accuses cops of digital tracking
Article Text:
Abhishek Upadhyay on Tuesday sought Supreme Court's intervention

Abhishek Upadhyay, the journalist who reported embezzlement of donations at Ayodhya's Ram temple, on Tuesday sought Supreme Court's intervention saying that Ghaziabad police have, in connection with a case of road rage against him, sought his digital footprints from social media platform X since June 1, which could jeopardise identities of sources who tipped him about the donation scam.His counsel Anoop P Awasthi told a bench led by CJI Surya Kant that Ghaziabad police's request to X HQ in California for the alleged road rage case of Aug 18 would result in gross violation of his right to privacy, adding that such data in the hands of police would reveal the identities of the sources who informed him about temple theft.The FIR concerns an alleged incident of Aug 18, yet the investigating agency seeks the petitioner's IP and account-related information from June 1, well before the alleged incident. No nexus between such sweeping historical digital information and the investigation of the alleged incident has been disclosed in the impugned notice," Upadhyay said in his application.The bench said it had on Aug 25 protected the journalist from coercive action by police in the road rage case and that his fresh application would be listed for hearing in due course.
Article Summary: Abhishek Upadhyay reported embezzlement of donations at Ayodhya's Ram temple. Ghaziabad police have, in connection with a case of road rage against him, sought his digital footprints from social media platform X since June 1.

Article Title: Bus gang-rape case: At minor’s UP village, locked house, silence and a family fleeing intrusion

AGRA: Fearing intrusion and social stigma, parents of the 17-year-old survivor in the Noida-Delhi bus gang-rape case have locked their house and left their UP village.A villager, who knows the family, toldon Tuesday: “After media persons began visiting our remote village in Mainpuri district seeking details about that horrific incident, they couldn’t take it anymore.” He added: “There’s no one in that house now, the dwelling has fallen silent. ”Another neighbour added: “No one here knew what had happened to the girl. When media persons came here on Monday and told us that she had been raped, everyone was shocked.” He appealed to journalists to avoid repeatedly visiting the place, citing concerns over the survivor’s future and privacy.“Please don’t come again and again to shoot videos or take pictures. She will have to get married in future. By revealing the village and asking people about her, the media has made the matter known here and also the neighbouring areas,” he added.The girl was allegedly sexually assaulted on a moving bus by the vehicle’s driver and conductor on Aug 4. The bus had travelled almost 50 km from Greater Noida to Old Delhi’s Kashmere Gate without being detected. The alleged sexual assault took place while she was travelling from Greater Noida towards Sector 63, police said.After violating her, the bus driver and conductor allegedly dumped her at Ring Road in the Kashmere Gate police station area. The accused duo were later identified as Kuldeep, 39 (bus driver); and Sandeep , 26 (conductor).The area’s SHO told: “The family is safe and have gone to their relatives.”Local MLA, who visited the village on Monday, said, “People in the village came to know about it probably yesterday. When I went there, I found her house locked. Her father’s phone was switched off. I made considerable efforts to speak with the family, but I have been unable to do so thus far.”The MLA added: “I demand the strictest possible punishment for the two accused.” Meanwhile, president of UP State Women Commission, Babita Chauhan, has written to police commissioner of Gautam Budh Nagar for “tough action”.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Bombay high court orders CBI probe into Sushant Singh Rajput’s ex-manager’s death
Article Text:
The HC said a senior officer of the CBI to conduct the probe.

Also Read |

Also Read |





MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Wednesday pronounced its judgment in the Disha Salian case and directed registration of a first information report (FIR) for her June 8, 2020 death at a suburban Malad building in Mumbai.The Bombay HC appointed a senior officer of the CBI to conduct the probe. The HC also directed not to name anyone as accused in the FIR.“No one shall be treated as an accused unless and until there is suitable material against them, the HC directed.Salian, 28, was a celebrity manager and worked with the late film actor Sushant Singh who died just days later that month on June 14, aged 34 in his Bandra house.On Friday Justices SV Kotwal and RR Bhonsale had reserved for orders her father Satish Salian’s petition to probe her death as a murder arguing through his counsel Nilesh Ojha that “suspicious circumstances’ surrounded it.He had sought investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and said the HC did not lack powers to direct registration of an FIR and probe to ensure complete justice for her family.On Wednesday the HC said : The officer is attached to CBI senior officer in this case and register the FIR, no one be detained unless there's a reasonable suspicion raised, BNSS and Summary report be filed if nothing is found.”At a three day hearing the bench repeatedly questioned the State on why it was still conducting an inquiry under section 174 of the erstwhile criminal procedure code (CrPC)—a provision which it said had limited applicability. The purpose of section 174/175 is limited to ascertaining ‘cause of death’ , as the first line of probe on registration of an Accidental Death Report (ADR).The inquiry that was closed within three months was reopened in 2023 following social media claims, prompting the HC to question the validity of such an extended inquiry.The State represented by chief public prosecutor Shishir Hirey maintained her death was by suicide, following an alleged fall from allegedly the 12th floor of the residential building.Salian’s petition claimed former chief minister Uddhav Thackeray’s son Aditya Thackeray to be an alleged suspect. Salian’s counsel Ojha citing documents, alleged discrepancies and suspicious circumstances to seek a thorough probe as he argued a cognizable offence as claimed by her father, ought to be registered as an FIR as mandated by law.The HC on being shown documents including the Panchanama, photographs of the body, other details from the inquiry so far and raised questions on various aspects it said were “suspicious’’ including whether injuries were consistent with a fall from such height and details regarding clothes.Hirey argued that the injuries included a skull fracture consistent with such fall. Hirey also sought to justify the ADR level inquiry and submitted witness statements and forensics which he said ruled out foul play or any alleged sexual assault on her.The HC clarified that it was not drawing conclusions at this stage but questioned the what had State done for so long jn the last five years, when the prosecution sought dismissal of the father’s plea saying it was belatedly filed .Senior counsel Sudeep Pasbola appearing for Thackeray who had intervened in the matter said the State’s line of probe was not barred by law but also cannot extend indefinitely. Pasbola said Salian has an alternate remedy in law to first go to Magistrate with a private complaint if no FIR is registered and could not directly come to the HC. Pasbola also argued that allegations agaisnt Thackeray were “motivated’’ untenable and stem from a “political rivalry’’.The HC said it was concerned not with any political overtones but only with sanctity of law to provide the family a closure. Ojha argued since the plea was for CBI probe the HC had to be approached as a magistrate lacks the power to direct such probe.Four-and-a half years after it began probing the death of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, last March, the CBI was reported to have closed the case and given a clean chit to actor Rhea Chakraborty, bringing curtains on the case that had gripped the country in 2020.Last year Satish Salian also alleged his daughter was sexually assaulted and murdered and had approached HC seeking the CBI probe into her death as he also alleged both deaths are interconnected and part of a larger conspiracy.
Article Summary: The Bombay HC appointed a senior officer of the CBI to conduct the probe. The HC also directed not to name anyone as accused in the FIR. Justices SV Kotwal and RR Bhonsale had reserved for orders her father Satish Salian’s petition to probe her death as a murder.

Article Title: Times Square stabbing: Bank of America VP Erin Piacenti among victims
Article Text:
NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch said the attack appeared to be random and unprovoked. Police said officers arriving at the scene encountered Pamela Cisneros, 49, who was brandishing two large knives and advancing towards them

Who was Erin Piacenti?

How the incident unfolded

A 32-year-old vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing incident in New York’s Times Square. The attack, described by police as “random” and unprovoked, unfolded on Monday afternoon.The victim was identified as Erin Piacenti, who was walking home from work when she was attacked near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue. Piacenti had recently returned to work after becoming a mother and had shared a photo of herself with her newborn daughter and husband four days before the stabbing.A 68-year-old man was also stabbed in the attack and was in stable condition, according to police. The attacker, identified as 49-year-old Pamela Cisneros, was shot and killed by officers after she advanced towards them while carrying two large knives.Piacenti was a vice-president in Bank of America’s Business Selection and Conflicts unit and had joined the company around 18 months ago, according to an internal memo and her LinkedIn profile.Matthew Koder, Bank of America’s president of Global Corporate & Investment Banking, described Piacenti as a “cherished teammate and friend” in an internal memo.“Erin was a valued member of the Business Selection and Conflicts team, having joined the bank 18 months ago,” Koder wrote.“Her loss is being felt deeply by many.”Bank of America confirmed Piacenti’s death and expressed condolences to her family.“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones,” the bank said in a statement.Piacenti had earned a law degree from Fordham Law School, graduating in 2021 alongside her husband, Frank, according to the school. Fordham Law said in a statement it was heartbroken by her death.Bank of America’s Manhattan office is located at One Bryant Park, just a few blocks from the site of the stabbing.NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the attack appeared to be random and unprovoked. Police identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, 49, of Queens.According to Tisch, Cisneros pulled two knives from a shopping bag, stabbed the 68-year-old man and then attacked Piacenti. When officers arrived, they found Cisneros brandishing two large knives and advancing towards them.Officers used a stun gun and tried to persuade her to drop the weapons for several minutes, but she refused. Tisch said Cisneros told officers she “would rather kill” them. Two officers then shot her, and she was later pronounced dead.Tisch said Cisneros had a documented mental health history, with police encounters related to mental health in 2018 and 2019, but no arrest record in New York City.Cisneros’ brother, Patrick Peralta, told Gothamist that she had psychiatric problems for decades but was not aggressive. He said she had been taking medication and had been doing better in recent years, working on and off in a legal office.“We really don’t know how to express or how to explain why this happened," Peralta told Gothamist, expressing sympathy for Piacenti’s family and the injured man.Koder said Bank of America’s security teams were “fully engaged in supporting the police investigation here, and in addressing the ongoing safety and security of our offices and teammates”.
Article Summary: Erin Piacenti, 32, was walking home from work when she was attacked near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue. A 68-year-old man was also stabbed in the attack and was in stable condition, according to police. Police identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, 49, of Queens. She was shot and killed by officers after she advanced towards them while carrying two large knives.

LUCKNOW: The search committee tasked with selecting the next chief executive officer (CEO) of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has shortlisted three candidates, who are said to be from Uttar Pradesh The first CEO of the Ram temple is likely to be selected from among the three at a meeting of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust scheduled at the residence of Trust’s president Nritya Gopal Das in Maniramdas Chhavani on Wednesday.One of the shortlisted candidates is a retired military officer, said a source associated with the process.The three candidates have worked across different parts of the country and have been associated with govt bodies as well as major projects.However, none of them is a bureaucrat or a police officer, contrary to the speculations that Trust could appoint a retired civil servant or a former police officer to the top administrative role.Trust members held discussions on the panel and were satisfied with the credentials and suitability of all three candidates, the sources said.Trust is expected to select one person from the recommended panel and negotiate the remuneration package with the final choice on Wednesday before formally announcing the appointment.The CEO will oversee Trust’s administrative operations, including management of pilgrim facilities, coordination during major religious events and engagement with govt agencies and other stakeholders connected with the functioning of the temple complex and related services.The recommendations follow a comprehensive, technology-enabled recruitment exercise that began with 5,585 applications. The process included multiple rounds of screening, online interactions and in-person meetings with 16 finalists held in Ayodhya on Aug 11 and 12, according to people familiar with the process.The search and selection committee comprised retired Supreme Court judge Justice Pramod Kohli, retired Lt Gen Vishnu Kant Chaturvedi and retired nuclear scientist Suresh Haware, who earlier served as chairperson of Shri Saibaba Sansthan Trust in Shirdi.Kohli said the committee had selected the candidates after a detailed assessment and that Trust would take the final decision.“Among the three people we have selected, the Trust will decide on one person for the CEO’s post. I believe that with Lord Ram’s blessings, the entire process will be completed smoothly,” Kohli said.Search committee secretary Sameer Panda said the shortlisted candidates reflected “the highest calibre of institutional leadership, management expertise, integrity and vision” required for an institution of national and international significance.He said the final report had been submitted and an official announcement would be made in due course.Rejecting speculation about external influence, Panda said no political, religious or social organisation had interfered in the selection process. “No BJP, RSS, VHP or any other organisation ever interfered or recommended anyone’s names for the CEO post,” he said.
Article Summary: The search committee tasked with selecting the next chief executive officer (CEO) of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has shortlisted three candidates. One of the shortlisted candidates is a retired military officer, said a source associated with the process. The CEO will oversee Trust’s administrative operations, including management of pilgrim facilities.

Article Title: Started by a Muslim, a Kolkata Janmashtami turns ‘Hindu-only’
Article Text:
Biplab Bhattacharjee Pandal construction for Janmashtami underway at Kidderpore

KOLKATA: One of Kolkata’s more prominent Janmashtami celebrations in Mominpore — where most of the organisers have been Muslims, making it an example of the city’s multi-cultural spirit — is set to turn into a Hindu-only affair this year.Rakesh Singh, who was BJP ’s (losing) candidate from the Port assembly constituency this year, toldon Tuesday that the celebrations will be organised by “only Hindus” this year as Janmashtami is “a Hindu festival”.Singh, who counted himself as a Congress functionary and used to control Alipore zoo’s labour union as part of the Indian National Trade Union Congress (a Congress affiliate), said he believes in Vishwa Hindu Parishad ’s ideology that “religion belongs to individuals and festivals also belong to those individuals” and was critical of former CM Mamata Banerjee’s oft-repeated statement that “religion belongs to individuals but festivals belong to everyone”.This Janmashtami event, held at the Bhukailash Road-Hussain Shah Road crossing in Kolkata Municipal Corporation’s Ward 79 — part of the Port assembly constituency and bordering CM Suvendu Adhikari’s and former CM Mamata Banerjee’s Bhowanipore constituency — enters its 58th year this time. Prominent patrons have included former city mayor Firhad Hakim and senior Trinamool functionaries Mohammed Alam and Serajul Karim.Singh’s “takeover” of the celebrations comes about a week after VHP addressed the city’s Durga Puja organisers on how to conduct Bengal’s biggest festival. Among the dos and don’ts listed were that there should be no distortion of deities’ images and pandals should be designed to maintain Hindu culture and heritage. VHP also asked puja organisers to strictly prohibit non-vegetarian food inside the core pandal area citing the need to maintain spiritual purity and cleanliness.Singh, who claimed to be both president and chairperson of the Janmashtami organising committee, said, “We cannot demean our traditional culture. People from other religions should definitely visit pandals but it is our duty to protect our religious activities. Janmashtami is a Hindu festival and it should be performed by Hindus only.”According to locals, the Janmashtami event, which is organised by Kidderpore Samaj Kalyan Samity, was initiated by a Muslim social worker, Md Kashim, about six decades ago but faded over the years till another group of Muslim youths revived it after Trinamool came to office in 2011.“Since 2011, we have been organising Janmashtami here. There were around 20 members in the organising committee, and half of them were Muslims. We used to celebrate the event together, distribute prasad and ensure all rituals were followed. But this year, all Muslim faces have been kept out of the committee,” said Md Alam, a Trinamool functionary and former office-bearer of the organising committee.On Monday,found a huge saffron-and-white pandal being erected at the venue. “Muslims used to control Janmashtami here till last year. But this year, it will be exclusively conducted and managed by Hindus. It’s like a cleansing activity,” said an organiser overseeing the pandal construction.
Article Summary: Rakesh Singh, who was BJP ’s (losing) candidate from the Port assembly constituency this year, toldon Tuesday that the celebrations will be organised by ‘only Hindus’ Singh said he believes in Vishwa Hindu Parishad’s ideology that ‘religion belongs to individuals and festivals also belong to those individuals’

Article Title: India on board, SCO reiterates condemnation of Iran attacks
Article Text:
SCO member-states, including India, reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on Iranian territory

India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Expressing deep concern over developments in "the Middle East and around Iran", the SCO member-states including India reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on Iranian territory that resulted in numerous civilian casualties and significant damage to Iran's economy, said the Bishkek Declaration.India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei.This was the second time that the SCO denounced the strikes on Iran after the West Asia war started on February 28, the first in an early March standalone statement that called the attacks unacceptable. India had endorsed that statement too, even though bilaterally it has not explicitly condemned the attacks on Iran the way it has missile and drone strikes on the GCC countries.However, unlike the Tianjin Declaration last year that too condemned the June 2025 US and Israeli strikes on Iran, the Bishkek Declaration did not name the US and Israel."Such actions violate the principles and norms of international law and the UN Charter and create serious risks to international peace, security and stability," said SCO's Bishkek Declaration.India and others backed Iran's sovereignty and territorial integrity, advocating a resolution to the conflict solely through political and diplomatic means.In this regard, they welcome all efforts aimed at de-escalating the situation in the region and, as the declaration said, noted that the only possible way to ensure peace and stability in the Middle East is a comprehensive and just settlement of the Palestinian question.PM Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek on Monday and backed expansion of bilateral economic ties with Tehran, while the Iranian president sought India's help to end the war. After distancing itself from a statement by SCO in June last year condemning Israel's strikes, India has signed on to joint documents by the bloc censuring US-Israel military action against Iran.The Declaration reflected a major Indian concern as it strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, emphasised that "double standards" in the fight against terrorism are unacceptable, and called on the international community to combat terrorism, including the cross-border movement of terrorists.It called for the UN playing a central role by fully implementing relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy in accordance with the UN Charter and the principles of international law to jointly combat all terrorist groups."Member States, reaffirming their firm commitment to combating terrorism, separatism, and extremism, emphasize the inadmissibility of attempts to exploit terrorist, separatist, and extremist groups for selfish purposes. They recognize the leading role of sovereign states and their competent authorities in countering terrorist and extremist threats," said the Declaration.Significantly, targeting use of economic sanctions by the West, the leaders came out in support of an open, fair and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system focused heavily on the framework established by the WTO, while slamming unilateral coercive measures."Member States oppose unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to the UN Charter and other norms of international law, the rules and principles of the World Trade Organization, that are detrimental to the interests of ensuring international security, including its food, energy and humanitarian components, and that have a negative impact on the global economy," said the Bishkek Declaration.
Article Summary: India joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei. This was the second time that the SCO denounced the strikes on Iran after the West Asia war started on February 28. India had endorsed that statement too, even though bilaterally it has not explicitly condemned the attacks on Iran.

Article Title: SC: Why not use 'totaliser' to mix votes?
Article Text:
Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different EVMs before counting, to prevent any backlash from candidates by preserving voter anonymity.Petitioner advocate Ashwini Upadhyay said a totalisation system hides booth-wise voting patterns by mixing up votes from multiple electronic voting machines (typically around 14) before displaying the count, which helps protect voters from post-poll violence and political victimisation. Election Commission , through senior advocate D Seshadri Naidu, said the issue was referred by EC to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ the 'totalisation' mechanism, mainly because of staunch opposition by political parties. He said a switch to this method would require changing the statute which the commission could not bring about.When Upadhyay pointed out that the totalisation mechanism was adopted by EC to count paper ballots, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked Centre to respond on why the same mechanism could not be adopted for EVMs. Upadhyay also said in Jan 2018, EC itself had told the court that the "time had come" to introduce the totaliser to "protect secrecy of the ballot and privacy of the individual".It had said that "the right of the people staying in a particular locality should not be exposed, and any kind of prejudice or discrimination because of the voting pattern should be avoided".In a U-turn, EC in its affidavit filed on Aug 31 said, "Experience of litigations has revealed that the present system which includes a simultaneous audit by the candidates is necessary to ensure that frivolous and baseless allegations do not cloud the outcome..." It said the introduction of the totaliser system would give fresh anxieties, misgivings and allegations regarding data, machine tampering and transmission glitches.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different EVMs before counting. Election Commission said the issue was referred by EC to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ 'totalisation' mechanism.

Article Title: NIA court orders attachment of accused’s property share in J&K terror-arms case
Article Text:
A special NIA court has ordered the attachment of the share of accused Fayaz Ahmed Mir in multiple properties in Kashmir

JAMMU: A special NIA court has ordered the attachment of the share of accused Fayaz Ahmed Mir in multiple properties in Kashmir while the trial in an alleged terror-linked arms case remains pending. Special Judge Prem Sagar passed the order Monday while allowing NIA’s application filed under Section 33(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, officials said.The properties listed in the order include 15 marlas (1 marla = 272.2sqft) of residential land, two shops spread over 2 marlas, and agricultural land measuring 25 marlas in Bumhama village of north Kashmir’s Baramulla district.The court directed that no third-party interest be created in the properties until the trial is over. The attachment applies only to Mir’s share in the listed properties and will remain in force until the proceedings conclude. A copy of the order has been forwarded to the Baramulla deputy commissioner for compliance, officials said.“Investigators alleged that Mir supplied arms, ammunition, and explosives to terrorists operating in south Kashmir, and received Rs 5.2 lakh in connection with an AK-47 rifle. The allegations are yet to be adjudicated by the trial court,” an official said.Mir’s counsel had opposed the attachment, arguing that the accused and his siblings had jointly inherited the properties, which were neither acquired through nor used for terrorist activities. The court, however, held that UAPA Section 33(1) permits attachment of property belonging to an accused facing trial for specified offences under the Act as a preventive measure.According to the case records, security forces intercepted a four-wheeler on the Srinagar-Jammu highway in Kulgam on Jan 11, 2020, and seized an AK-47 rifle, three pistols, a hand grenade and other incriminating materials. The occupants were identified as J&K Police DSP Devender Singh; Hizbul Mujahideen members Irfan Shafi Mir alias Advocate, Syed Naveed Mushtaq alias Naveed Babu and Rafi Ahmad Rather; former LoC trader Tanveer Ahmad Wani, and Naveed Babu’s brother Syed Irfan Ahmad. Four suspects, including two Hizbul terrorists, were arrested.
Article Summary: The properties listed in the order include 15 marlas (1 marla = 272.2sqft) of residential land, two shops spread over 2 marlas, and agricultural land measuring 25 marlas. Mir’s counsel had opposed the attachment, arguing that the accused and his siblings had jointly inherited the properties.

NEW DELHI: An unexpected roadside interaction between Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay and an elderly woman became one of the notable moments of his visit to Mettur in Salem district on Tuesday. NEW DELHI: The political row over an alleged “fish feast” at a Congress event in Ayodhya escalated on Tuesday, with Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai filing a defamation case against Yogi Adityanath , alleging that the chief minister's remarks had “hurt his faith.”Rai approached the MP-MLA court in Lucknow, the UP Cong chief also denied eating fish at the event, saying he is a vegetarian. “We do not eat non-vegetarian food. The allegation of a fish feast against me is wrong. The chief minister's statement has hurt my faith,” Rai told ANI.Rai said he had filed the defamation case to seek legal action and challenged the chief minister to produce evidence in court.“Yogi cast aspersions on my character and my dietary habits; he claimed that I visit Hanuman Garhi, apply the tilak and sandalwood paste, and pay obeisance to Lord Ram, only to subsequently feast on fish. The fact is, we are not non-vegetarians; we hail from Kashi, the city of Baba Vishwanath. The chief minister levelled a false allegation. I have filed a defamation suit here today. If the CM possesses evidence, he should present it in court and prove whether I am in the wrong or he is,” Rai said.Explaining his presence at the event, Rai said he had been invited to a fish feast organised by the Nishad community and attended it out of respect for the organisers.“I was invited to a fish feast organised by the Nishad community, a community whose livelihood involves rearing, selling, and consuming fish. I would not disrespect or insult anyone's event, so I attended and participated. He alleged that I consumed fish during the month of Sawan. I believe such tactics are characteristic of the BJP, not us,” Rai added.The remarks came days after Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath launched a sharp attack on Rai over the alleged incident at an Ayodhya programme organised by members of the Nishad community.The controversy erupted after a video showing fish being prepared at the Congress event surfaced on social media during the month of Shravan, when many Hindus observe dietary restrictions.The event was held to welcome Rai, who had attended a programme organised by the Nishad community. The issue quickly became political, with the BJP targeting Rai over the alleged feast and the Congress rejecting the allegations.Addressing a gathering in Raebareli on August 24, Adityanath accused Rai of “duplicity” for visiting Hanumangarhi to offer prayers and later attending a programme where fish was allegedly served.“You saw the behaviour of the Congress state president: he goes to offer prayers at Hanumangarhi, but later outside he enjoys a feast of fish. He could have eaten whatever he wanted outside-anywhere other than Ayodhya. Yet, this is the duplicity they display,” Adityanath said.“Even a chameleon would be put to shame by these people; it would wonder what kind of human species this is-chanting 'Ram-Ram' inside the temple and feasting on fish the moment they step out,” he added.The chief minister also accused Rai of not standing up to mafia elements in the past and referred to the killing of his brother, former MLA Awadhesh Rai.“When a mafia don murdered his brother, this man did not testify against the criminal; instead, he knelt and bowed in submission before him,” he added.Rai had earlier challenged Adityanath to produce evidence of him eating fish. In an open letter to the chief minister on August 28, he said he was a vegetarian and would quit politics if proof was produced.“It is an immutable truth that I am a vegetarian. If you have any authenticated photograph or video of me eating fish, make it public. I will retire from politics,” Rai said.He said five days had passed since he issued the challenge but there had been no response. Rai also rejected Adityanath’s allegations about his alleged links with mafia elements, citing his nearly 32-year legal battle following the killing of his brother.He accused the state government of focusing on personal and provocative remarks instead of issues such as law and order, crimes against women and weaker sections, unemployment, inflation, farmers’ concerns, electricity supply, roads and alleged corruption.“My humble but clear advice is to stop making false and unsubstantiated statements and focus on the real problems of Uttar Pradesh,” Rai added.
Article Summary: U.S. Congress president Ajay Rai files defamation case against Uttar Pradesh chief minister. Yogi Adityanath accused Rai of 'duplicity' over alleged 'fish feast' at event in Ayodhya. Rai says he is a vegetarian and challenged the chief minister to produce evidence in court.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday invoked its special powers and quashed all FIRs registered against student protesters in different parts of the country during the NEET paper leak protests.The bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana said the order had been passed in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and shall not be treated as a precedent.The apex court said it was invoking its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution considering the future of the students who bona fide participated in the protests.The court, however, allowed Delhi Police to pursue the FIR against 2,873 individuals who were present at the Jantar Mantar protests, citing their serious criminal antecedents.This comes a day after the Centre moved the apex court seeking to quash FIRs registered against student protesters over alleged violence during protests against the NEET paper leak in Delhi and other states.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, also informed the apex court that the Centre remained committed to fulfilling all three assurances given to CJP leaders during their meeting with the government.Under the first assurance, the Centre would not pursue FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25. The second was that no fresh FIRs would be registered in connection with the matter.The third assurance was that the government would provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak."The Centre is committed to honouring the assurance given to CJP leaders to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after the NEET exam cancellation; however, three months are needed to work out the modalities," Mehta told the Supreme Court."As of now, we are committed to fulfilling all three assurances," he added.Following the apex court hearing, Cockroach Janata Party called off its September 5 protest against the Centre for failing to honour the promises made to persuade the group to withdraw the agitation."I want to state that in view of the positive assurances of the Government of India and the judicial sanctity bestowed upon them today, and in view of the order being passed by this court, the CJP deems it appropriate to withdraw the call for the march on September 5 and looks forward to compliance with today's order," CJP co-convener Sourav Das said during a hearing in the Supreme Court.After the hearing, Das said welcomed SC's order but also questioned why were these 'hardend criminals' allowed to roam freely in the society in the first place."Regarding the Delhi Police’s apprehension, based on facial recognition technology, that around 2,800 alleged hardened criminals were present at the protest site, we argued during negotiations with the government that if these 2,800 hardened criminals were indeed present, the first question was why they were roaming freely in society in the first place," Das said while talking to reporters."Secondly, if they committed any heinous crimes, such as rape, murder, or other grave offences, at the protest site, then they should be prosecuted, investigated, and imprisoned," he added.During a hearing on August 18 on petitions related to the student protests, Supreme Court had indicated that it was inclined to quash the FIRs by exercising its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution.The indication came after the court was informed of legal complications in withdrawing the FIRs. Once registered, the cases can be closed only through a closure report, which the concerned Magistrate has the discretion to reject.Earlier, Supreme Court had also constituted a committee to examine allegations of excessive use of force by security personnel against students during the July 20 march over the NEET paper leak.
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Tuesday invoked its special powers and quashed all FIRs registered against student protesters in different parts of the country. The court, however, allowed Delhi Police to pursue the FIR against 2,873 individuals who were present at the Jantar Mantar protests. Cockroach Janata Party called off its September 5 protest against the Centre for failing to honour the promises made to persuade the group to withdraw the agitation.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said there can be no “double standards” in the fight against terrorism and called for dismantling its entire ecosystem, including financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.Addressing the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, PM Modi described terrorism as a “grave challenge to all of humanity” and said the fight against it cannot be limited to a mindset of “action-reaction”.“We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism--its financing, recruitment, radicalization, and safe havens. We must speak in one voice that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,” he said.“Those countries that use terrorism as an instrument of their policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism cannot be a ‘strategic asset’ for anyone,” the Prime Minister added.He also outlined "Security, Connectivity and Opportunity" as the three pillars of India’s vision for the SCO, with peace and security forming the first pillar.“Our shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan,” he said, adding that India would continue its development and humanitarian assistance to the Afghan people.On the West Asia crisis, Modi said conflicts in one region can have repercussions across the world, affecting “energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains of the entire world”.“The countries of the Global South have to bear the maximum brunt of this. Therefore, India's call has been that the solution to all tensions and wars is not possible on the battlefield, but only through Dialogue and Diplomacy,” he said.The Prime Minister also flagged drug trafficking as a serious threat to the younger generation and regional security, calling for stronger cooperation through SCO mechanisms dealing with security threats, organised crime, information security and narcotics. “We must make them effective mediums for practical coordination and timely action,” PM Modi said.He further stressed that SCO cooperation should translate into tangible benefits for people, with people-to-people ties placed at the centre of the grouping’s future agenda.“The true measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts have created for young people, how many new markets have opened up for our entrepreneurs, how much our farmers have benefited from technology, and how much better the lives of our citizens have become,” he said.Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov is hosting the summit and serving as its chairman. PM Modi is attending alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other leaders of SCO member states.
Article Summary: PM Modi called for dismantling the entire ecosystem that enables terrorism at SCO Summit. He outlined "Security, Connectivity and Opportunity" as the three pillars of India’s vision for the SCO. He also flagged drug trafficking as a serious threat to the younger generation.

NEW DELHI: Amid continuing reverberations from Rahul Gandhi ’s girl-students rally in Pune, the Congress youth outreach “Chhatron ki Goonj” is set to move to another BJP stronghold, the education hub of Madhya Pradesh.Sources said the next episode of “chhatron ki goonj” will be held in Indore on Sep 12.In what is a carefully crafted strategy to challenge the ruling party with the “angry demographic” that led the Jantar Mantar protest, Congress has picked the venue owing to the fact that there has been a history of paper leaks in the state including the infamous examination scandal “Vyapam scam”. Besides, the opposition has won two by-elections “against the might of the state”, the latest being Datia assembly last month.Sources said the party considered a few cities, including in the Congress-ruled states in the south, but then decided on Indore in a bid to continue pressuring the BJP.While the city is a students’ hub and also has a fair share of urban and middle-class population, it has been in the negative spotlight for repeated infrastructural crises – the most sensational being 24 deaths from consuming sewage contaminated water in February 2026.A smart city road, said to be constructed at the cost of Rs 40 crore, collapsed recently, hogging the headlines. Also, there have been allegations of corruption targeting the CM.The “chhatron ki goonj” started in Kota in Rajasthan (June) and then moved to Dehradun (July) and then Prayagraj (August), focusing on examination and employment issues. But in Pune last month, Rahul changed tack when he made it an exclusive event for girls, and his interactive speech around gender justice and “manusmriti” received favourable feedback besides triggering the opponent BJP.The “CKG” strategists are chuffed by the reaction and said the programme will move across the nation with the objective of becoming a “brand” that the youth will associate with.After Indore, the party may choose a city in any of the Congress-ruled states in the south to cover a key region with a strong youth population.Recently, the Congress Working Committee decided that “CKG” will be held in 800 cities and towns – which means one in every district. Sources said Rahul may personally attend around 20 of them, while the rest will become a vehicle for the party to woo the youth.

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.

Judge must get fair chance to respond: CJI Surya Kant

NEW DELHI: Responding to letters written by SC judge Sandeep Mehta complaining against Rajasthan high court acting chief justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and seeking his transfer outside the state, CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response.Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.Justice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC.CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said. He also released a public statement Wednesday decrying the attempt to hold a public trial over allegations made by one judge against another.Contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in public domain and that judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion is reached.The fact that allegations have been made, therefore, cannot by itself be treated as a finding against the judge,” CJI Surya Kant’s statement said.The established mechanism for inquiring into allegations of an Supreme Court or High Court judge is the constitution of an in-house committee — comprising judges — by the Chief Justice of India, if he finds the response of the judge accused of misdemeanour or corrupt practices unsatisfactory and feels the charges are serious enough to warrant a deeper probe.CJI Kant, who is on a three-day official visit to Germany, also told TOI that he has already sought a response from Justice Sharma following the letters from Justice Mehta, who has alleged that there is “clear evidence of favouritism” by Justice Sharma. Justice Mehta’s complaints are being examined, CJI Surya Kant said.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response. Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26. CJI Kant: “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media’

Article Title: No intention to quit politics, Nitin Gadkari clarifies

Article Title: Hong Kong’s pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty to association with foreign entities
Article Text:
Pro-democratic student activist Joshua Wong, on Sept. 2, 2015. (Photo: AP)

Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong, 29, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to a national security allegation of collusion with foreign entities, an offence that carries a potential life sentence. Several Western diplomats were present at the hearing.Wong rose to international prominence as a teenage pro-democracy activist, part of a generation of young protesters whose activism has since been effectively criminalised under the sweeping National Security Law that Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020.According to a charge sheet seen by Reuters, prosecutors accused Wong of conspiring with exiled activist Nathan Law and others to solicit foreign countries, institutions, organisations, or individuals to impose sanctions or blockades against Hong Kong and China. The alleged conduct occurred between July 1 and November 23, 2020. Wong was arrested on these charges in June 2025, the second time he has faced prosecution under the National Security Law.During the hearing, prosecutors emphasised an alleged international media and political campaign led by Demosisto, a now-disbanded political party Wong once led, that had advocated for a referendum on Hong Kong's sovereignty.The campaign reportedly sought sanctions against Hong Kong and China in 2019 and 2020.Wong is currently serving a sentence from an earlier national security conviction, conspiracy to commit subversion, stemming from his participation in an unofficial 2020 primary election among democratic activists. That sentence is due to end next year.The National Security Law was enacted on June 30, 2020, partly in response to the often-violent pro-democracy protests that engulfed Hong Kong in 2019.International human rights organisations and Western governments have criticised the law as excessive, arguing it undermines the high degree of autonomy promised to Hong Kong after its 1997 handover from British to Chinese rule.Hong Kong and Chinese authorities, however, maintain the law was necessary to restore stability.
Article Summary: Joshua Wong, 29, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to a national security allegation of collusion with foreign entities. The offence carries a potential life sentence. Wong rose to international prominence as a teenage pro-democracy activist. His activism has since been effectively criminalised under the sweeping National Security Law.

Article Title: ‘We would have had real civil strife’: JD Vance recalls 2024 attack on Trump
Article Text:
US Vice President JD Vance

Vance on Trump's AI-generated image as Jesus Christ

US Vice President JD Vance said in a podcast released Tuesday (local time) that he feared a “real civil strife” had a 2024 attempt on Donald Trump ’s life been successful.Vance made the remarks during a conversation with Christian podcaster Bryce Crawford. During the conversation, he cited the July 13, 2024, assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, during which a bullet whizzed past Trump’s ear before striking a supporter, who was killed. The gunman, Thomas Matthew Crooks, was shot dead by Secret Service snipers.“We would have had real civil strife in a way that I don't know that the country could have ever come back from. There would have just been an illegitimacy to our entire political system,” the Associated Press quoted the vice president as saying.Vance further stated that, like many other Trump supporters, he too would have suspected a conspiracy had Crooks been successful.“I would have assumed very dark forces had taken out Donald Trump, right as he was about to come back into the White House. Many Trump supporters would have assumed a conspiracy had robbed them of their chosen president... I would have also had those thoughts 'in the back of my mind,'” he added.On July 15, 2024, Trump formally announced Vance as his running mate, or vice presidential candidate. In the November 2024 election, the Trump-Vance Republican ticket defeated the Democratic ticket of Kamala Harris and her running mate, Tim Walz.Crawford also asked Vance about a social media post Trump shared earlier this year featuring an AI-generated image of himself as Jesus, which the podcast host described as offensive. Trump initially contended that he thought the image depicted him as a doctor, but later removed the post amid widespread criticism, including from some of his own supporters.Vance defended the president, arguing that Trump did not intend to “mock or mimic God” and that “that's just not who he is.” He added that Trump often tries to keep things light and frequently jokes. “He's a bit of a ballbuster, for those of us who work with him, and he just likes to have a good time,” Vance remarked. “And I think that if people appreciated that, they would recognize, he's not trying to offend people, he's trying to keep things light. ”
Article Summary: US Vice President JD Vance made the remarks during a conversation with Christian podcaster Bryce Crawford. Vance cited the July 13, 2024, assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, during which a bullet whizzed past Trump’s ear before striking a supporter, who was killed.

Article Title: Two injured in explosion at railway station in Germany’s Augsburg
Article Text:
The station has been completely shut down and rail services suspended (File photo)

Two people sustained minor injuries after an unidentified object exploded at a train station in the southern German city of Augsburg, local media reported.Window panes were also damaged in the explosion, which occurred in a passageway inside the station.Police responded to the incident at around 5 am local time and cordoned off parts of the station as officers investigated the scene. An explosive-disposal robot was also deployed.The station was later completely shut down and rail services were suspended after police described the object as “suspicious”, without providing further details. Earlier, one track had remained operational.Augsburg is a regional transport hub located around 55 km (35 miles) west of Munich, Germany’s third-largest city after capital Berlin and Hamburg.
Article Summary: Window panes were also damaged in the explosion, which occurred in a passageway inside the station. The station was later completely shut down and rail services were suspended. Police described the object as ‘suspicious’, without providing further details.

Article Title: Two Turkish ships collide off Istanbul; one believed sunk, 10 crew missing
Article Text:
10 crew members aboard one of the vessels are unreachable (Representative image)
